**Swipe on what to watch next, alone or with a group.**

`MIT` · `Next` · `SQLite` · `v2.3.0` · `ghcr.io/jakobbjelver/messer-swipe`
<!-- /messer:hero -->

Swipe turns "what should we watch?" into a deck everyone can agree on. One person creates a session, the
others join from a phone, and the app finds the titles two people liked — or that everyone did.

It works with the media server you already run (Jellyfin, Plex, Emby) or standalone against TMDB, with
no server at all. Mobile-first, installable, and it keeps its own tiny SQLite database of sessions,
swipes and matches.

## Run

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name messer-swipe \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 4321:4321 \
  -v "$PWD/messer-swipe-data:/app/data" \
  -e PROVIDER=jellyfin \
  -e JELLYFIN_URL=http://your-jellyfin:8096 \
  ghcr.io/jakobbjelver/messer-swipe:latest
```

Then open `http://localhost:4321`. Or build it yourself: `npm ci && npm run build && npm start` after
`npm run db:migrate` (`make docker` builds the image the CI publishes).

`AUTH_SECRET` is generated on first boot and stored beside the database when unset; set it explicitly if
you run more than one replica. For HTTPS set `USE_SECURE_COOKIES=true` and `APP_PUBLIC_URL` to the
hostname that serves the app — it drives canonical URLs, the OG image, `robots.txt` and secure cookies.

A hosted demo runs at **[swipe.messer.wtf](https://swipe.messer.wtf)** in TMDB mode. One-click deploy to
Vercel: [clone with the Turso integration](https://vercel.com/new/clone?repository-url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fjakobbjelver%2Fmesser-swipe&env=PROVIDER,TMDB_ACCESS_TOKEN,USE_SECURE_COOKIES&envDefaults=%7B%22PROVIDER%22%3A%22tmdb%22%2C%22USE_SECURE_COOKIES%22%3A%22true%22%7D&project-name=messer-swipe).

## What it does

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **Providers** | Jellyfin and TMDB are the supported pair; Emby and Plex are experimental |
| **Shows** | series cards with seasons, episodes and the commitment numbers; a detail sheet that answers "where do I start" |
| **Deck modes** | movies, shows, whole shows or single episodes, what you are already watching, or both kinds mixed |
| **Sessions** | create or join in seconds from a link; no account for a guest |
| **Match rules** | "any two people" or "everyone must agree" |
| **Session limits** | cap likes, dislikes or total matches so a session ends |
| **Watchlist sync** | a match is written back to the media server you already use |
| **Mobile** | phone-first deck, installable as a PWA, keyboard shortcuts on a desktop |
| **Standalone** | TMDB mode needs no media server and no library |

**Two provider modes.** *Server lock* (`PROVIDER_LOCK=true`, the default) fixes the provider from the
environment: one server, one library, nothing to configure in the UI. *BYOP* (`PROVIDER_LOCK=false`) lets
each visitor point the app at their own server at runtime — private or LAN URLs stay refused unless you
set `ALLOW_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS=true`.

The variables that matter most:

| Variable | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `PROVIDER` | `jellyfin` | `jellyfin`, `plex`, `emby` or `tmdb` |
| `PROVIDER_LOCK` | `true` | `false` lets a visitor choose their own provider |
| `JELLYFIN_URL` / `PLEX_URL` / `EMBY_URL` | — | the server the app reads from |
| `TMDB_ACCESS_TOKEN` | — | required for `PROVIDER=tmdb` |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `file:/app/data/swiparr.db` | a SQLite path, or a Turso URL with `DATABASE_AUTH_TOKEN` |
| `APP_PUBLIC_URL` | `swipe.messer.wtf` | canonical host; set it to yours |
| `AUTH_SECRET` | generated | session and guest-lending keys, ≥ 32 chars |
| `USE_SECURE_COOKIES` | `false` | `true` behind HTTPS |
| `HIDE_PASSWORD_LOGIN` | `false` | hides the username/password form on a Jellyfin install that has Quick Connect — for SSO setups. Ignored on Plex, Emby and TMDB, which would otherwise have no way in |
| `MAX_IMAGE_WIDTH` | `960` | largest poster the client asks for |

The full matrix — including the image queue, security headers and admin usernames — is in
[`docs/configuration.md`](docs/configuration.md); what each deck mode does is in
[`docs/features.md`](docs/features.md). Upgrading from 1.x? Read [`docs/upgrading-to-2.0.md`](docs/upgrading-to-2.0.md)
first: it covers the one stored change (TMDB ids are typed in 2.0) and how to roll back.

## Contract

The app is a Next.js server with route handlers under `/api`: `auth`, `session`, `swipe`, `media`,
`user`, `events` (SSE for a live session), `admin`, `og`, `health` and `version`. Every failure answers
the same envelope, `{"error":{"code","message"}}`, and `GET /api/version` reports the build.

Sessions are the unit of state: a session owns its members, its swipes and its matches, and the deck is
computed per member from the provider's catalogue. There is no accounts system — a member is a name and
a signed cookie, and the admin is the first account that logs in on a provider that has accounts at all.

## Agents

Read [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) — the code contract, the invariants and the commands — then
[`docs/llms.txt`](docs/llms.txt), the primer for an agent that is about to change code. `npm run check`
(lint, typecheck, tests) is the gate; `npm run doctor` diagnoses a deployment; `npm run e2e` drives the
contract against a running instance.

To **operate** an instance with an agent rather than change its code, see [`docs/agents.md`](docs/agents.md):
the CLI ships inside the image, so `docker exec <container> messer-swipe status` is the whole setup.

Contributions are closed: no pull requests. **Issues and discussions are open** — bug reports and ideas
are read, and a bug with a reproduction gets fixed. A vulnerability goes to a private advisory, per
[`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md).

## Design notes

**The deck is a view, not a table.** Nothing is precomputed per user: the deck is a page of the
provider's catalogue filtered by what this member has already swiped. A session with 40 members costs
one query per member, not 40 tables.

**A match is a rule, not a majority.** "Any two" and "everyone" are the two rules that make group
watching actually work; a match record names the rule that produced it, so a surprising match is
explainable.

**One image budget.** Posters are fetched through the app, not hot-linked from the server, because a
slow media server must not make the deck feel broken: the queue is bounded by `IMAGE_CONCURRENCY`, each
fetch has a timeout, and a failure is a `504` the card retries — never a cached broken image.

## Status

Active. The supported path is Jellyfin and TMDB; Emby and Plex work and are labelled experimental
because their libraries differ in ways that still surprise the deck.
